name: Felix
bio: Felix, the Roman governor of Judea, received Paul in Caesarea under guard along with Claudius Lysias's letter explaining the charges against him; upon learning Paul was from Cilicia, Felix agreed to hear the case once his accusers arrived, and had him kept under guard in Herod's palace (Acts 23:24-35). His further dealings with Paul are told in the chapters ahead.  When the high priest Ananias and Tertullus accused Paul before him, Felix heard both sides and postponed judgment until Lysias could be consulted, granting Paul guarded liberty. Felix later sent for Paul with his wife Drusilla to hear him on faith in Christ, grew afraid at Paul's words on judgment, and kept delaying in hopes of a bribe, ultimately leaving Paul in prison for two years to please the Jews when Porcius Festus succeeded him (Acts 24:1-27).
